question.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Double Integral Over a Rectangular Domain
question.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{4},\,0\le y\le \pi \}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:   

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

Making a substitution $x+y=u,$ $\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ we get.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[{\int }_{y}^{y+\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡u\,\text{d}u]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[\operatorname{sin}⁡u]_{y}^{y+\pi /4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{sin}⁡y]\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }[\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{sin}⁡y]\text{d}y & ={[\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+\frac{\pi }{4})]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{4}))-(\operatorname{cos}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})) \\  & =(-1+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-(1-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =\sqrt{2}-2\end{aligned}
$$
